questions.question: The mean of the following distribution is 18: Classes: 11-13 (f=7), 13-15 (f=6), 15-17 (f=9), 17-19 (f=13), 19-21 (f=f_k), 21-23 (f=5), 23-25 (f=4). What is the value of the missing frequency f_k?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.1 Question 3

questions.question: If the difference between mode and median of a data distribution is 24, what is the difference between median and mean?
questions.explanation: Mode - Median = (3 Median - 2 Mean) - Median = 2 Median - 2 Mean = 2(Median - Mean). Therefore, 24 = 2(Median - Mean) => Median - Mean = 12.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.4

questions.question: For the data: (0-10: 5), (10-20: 12), (20-30: 20), (30-40: 15), (40-50: 8). What is the sum of the lower limit of the median class and the lower limit of the modal class?
questions.explanation: 1. Modal class: maximum frequency is 20, so modal class is 20-30. Lower limit = 20. 2. Median class: N = 5 + 12 + 20 + 15 + 8 = 60. N/2 = 30. Cumulative frequencies: 5, 17, 37, 52, 60. The class with cf >= 30 is 20-30. Lower limit = 20. Sum of lower limits = 20 + 20 = 40.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: A survey of 20 houses found the following plants per house: (0-2: 1), (2-4: 2), (4-6: 1), (6-8: 5), (8-10: 6), (10-12: 2), (12-14: 3). What is the mean number of plants per house?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.1 Question 1

questions.question: Ages of patients admitted in a hospital: 5-15 (6), 15-25 (11), 25-35 (21), 35-45 (23), 45-55 (14), 55-65 (5). What is the mode of the ages?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.2 Question 1

questions.question: The median of 100 observations is 525. Classes are 0-100 to 900-1000. If the median class is 500-600 with lower limit 500, class width 100, frequency 20, and cf of preceding class is 36 + x, what is the value of x?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.3 Question 2

questions.subtopic: Effect of Change of Origin and Scale
questions.question: If ui = (xi - 25) / 10, sum(fi * ui) = 20, and sum(fi) = 100, what is the arithmetic mean x̄?
questions.explanation: Assumed mean a = 25, class width h = 10. Mean x̄ = a + [sum(fi * ui) / sum(fi)] * h = 25 + (20 / 100) * 10 = 25 + 0.2 * 10 = 25 + 2 = 27.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.2

questions.question: Given cumulative distribution: Less than 10 (f=4), Less than 20 (f=11), Less than 30 (f=22), Less than 40 (f=35). What is the frequency of the class interval 20 - 30?
questions.explanation: Frequency of class 20-30 = (Cumulative frequency up to 30) - (Cumulative frequency up to 20) = 22 - 11 = 11.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.4

questions.question: Life of 225 electric components: 0-20 (10), 20-40 (35), 40-60 (52), 60-80 (61), 80-100 (38), 100-120 (29). What is the modal lifetime of the components?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.2 Question 2

questions.question: When computing the median of grouped data, which of the following is true regarding class widths?
options: Class intervals must strictly be of equal width
Class marks must be consecutive integers
Class intervals need not necessarily be equal, but must be continuous
questions.explanation: The formula for median requires only that the classes be made continuous and arranged in increasing order. In calculating median, h represents the width of the median class specifically, so unequal class widths elsewhere do not invalidate the median formula.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.4

questions.question: If Mode = 35.3 and Mean = 30.5, what is the value of the median using the empirical formula?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.4

questions.question: Lengths of 40 leaves are measured in mm: 118-126 (3), 127-135 (5), 136-144 (9), 145-153 (12), 154-162 (5), 163-171 (4), 172-180 (2). What is the lower limit of the median class after making classes continuous?
questions.explanation: Adjustment = 0.5. Continuous intervals: 117.5-126.5 (3), 126.5-135.5 (5, cf=8), 135.5-144.5 (9, cf=17), 144.5-153.5 (12, cf=29). N = 40, N/2 = 20. The cumulative frequency >= 20 is 29, so the median class is 144.5 - 153.5. Its lower limit is 144.5 mm.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.3 Question 4

questions.subtopic: Mean of First n Natural Numbers
questions.question: What is the arithmetic mean of the first n natural numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., n?
questions.explanation: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) / 2. Mean = Sum / n = [n(n + 1) / 2] / n = (n + 1) / 2.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.2

questions.question: If the mean of 5 observations x, x+2, x+4, x+6, x+8 is 11, what is the mean of the last three observations?
questions.explanation: Sum = 5x + 20. Mean = (5x + 20)/5 = x + 4 = 11 => x = 7. The 5 observations are 7, 9, 11, 13, 15. The last three observations are 11, 13, 15. Their mean is (11 + 13 + 15) / 3 = 39 / 3 = 13.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exemplar Problem

questions.question: A life insurance agent found the following data for ages of 100 policy holders: Below 20 (2), Below 25 (6), Below 30 (24), Below 35 (45), Below 40 (78), Below 45 (89). How many policy holders are in the age group 35 - 40?
questions.explanation: The frequency for the interval 35 - 40 is (Cumulative frequency below 40) - (Cumulative frequency below 35) = 78 - 45 = 33.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Exercise 13.3 Question 3

questions.question: In the assumed mean method, what is the best recommended choice for 'a' (assumed mean)?
options: The class mark of the central or middle class interval
The lower limit of the first class
questions.explanation: Selecting 'a' as the class mark of the middle class interval keeps the deviations di both positive and negative, minimizing the magnitude of products fi*di and easing calculation.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.2

questions.question: Given fi: 4, 8, 14, 11, 3 for class marks xi: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. What is the mean?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.2

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Mode is correct?
options: Mode always takes every observation into account
Mode can never be determined graphically
A data distribution can never have more than one mode
Mode is not affected by extreme values (outliers) in the data set
questions.explanation: Mode is purely based on the highest frequency and is not influenced by extreme outliers at either tail of the distribution, unlike the arithmetic mean which is heavily sensitive to outliers.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.3

questions.question: If the intersection point of a less than ogive and a more than ogive is (28.5, 50), what is the median and the total number of observations N?
questions.explanation: The point of intersection of the two ogives is (Median, N/2). Therefore, Median = 28.5 and N/2 = 50, which gives total observations N = 2 * 50 = 100.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.4

questions.question: Under what condition is the step-deviation method strictly convenient to apply?
options: When all class frequencies are prime numbers
When all class intervals have equal class size h and deviations di have a common factor
When the class intervals have varying and unequal widths
questions.explanation: The step-deviation method is most convenient when all class intervals have equal width h, so that ui = (xi - a)/h results in small consecutive integers.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 13 Statistics, Section 13.2
